newsitem.title: DUBAI: Oman and South Korea to sign gas deal.
newsitem.headline: Oman and South Korea to sign gas deal.

text.p: Oman LNG LLC and Korea Gas Corp (Kogas) will sign a sale and purchase agreement for liquefied natural gas (LNG) on October 23 in Muscat, a statement from Oman LNG LLC said on Sunday.
"The agreement is for the supply of over four million tonnes of LNG per annum from Oman to Korea for 25 years," the statement received in Dubai said.
The contract with Korea Gas Corp is the backbone of the Gulf Arab country's $6 billion LNG project, the sultanate's largest industrial project.
Oman and South Korea reached the full sale and purchase agreement in August for a fob deal of 4.1 million tonnes of LNG with deliveries starting in early 2000.
Oman LNG Company -- responsible for the liquefaction plant, transportation and sales from the 6.6 million tonnes a year LNG project is 51 percent owned by the Omani government.
Shareholders are Royal Dutch Shell Group, Total SA six percent, Partex (Oman) Corp two percent, Mitsubishi Corp and Mistui and Co Ltd three percent each and ITOCHU Corp one percent.
